Items.Authors: Viljon Sekseni, Freerk Schütt, Kersten Mumme, Dhruti Mavani, Tobias Brunken, Mohamed Shehata, Miriam Brandt, Philipp Huke
Items.Title: Three-port Fourier-transform spectrometer for high precision differential measurements
Items.Abstract: To get a high resolution with a Fourier-transform Spectrometer (FTS) long paths are needed, even though a few cm already suffice to exceed resolutions of most echelle spectrographs. This allows to build compact FTS for monitoring calibration sources with high precision and accuracy when calibrated properly. The slow speed of the moving mirror(s) require a sophisticated detector-architecture. Especially for broad-band or incoherent sources strong averaging is needed to compensate for the small SNR outside the coherence length.  Here, we report about a FTS with three input-ports. Three input-ports allows to measure two ports in a differential mode, thereby using the third port for reference. This is particularly useful to measure differentially the behaviour of fibers. The detector architecture is based on fast, low-noise photodiodes with low amplification and a conventional ADC. The six output ports enhance the SNR and enable relatively fast measurement of broad-band light sources.

Items.Authors: Ahmed Sanny, Pradip Gatkine, Darshpreet Kaur Saini, Bibhudutta Rout, Hugo García-Vázquez, Diego Portero-Rodríguez, Luis Ramos, Nemanja Jovanovic
Items.Title: Toward space-qualification of astrophotonic spectrographs for space telescopes
Items.Abstract: Astrophotonics has rapidly matured into a key technology for ground-based observatories, replacing bulky optics with compact, stable photonic components for high-angular-resolution and high-contrast astronomy. As future space missions such as HWO and LIFE demand reliable photonic systems operating from the visible to the infrared, rigorous environmental qualification per NASA and ECSS standards is essential. This work presents a space-environment evaluation of near-infrared passive AWG-based spectrographs fabricated in doped-SiO₂ with square waveguides, compatible with future upgrades to active photonic integrated circuits. With a resolving power of ~200 over the 200–350 nm range, the devices are tested as standalone chips and packaged assemblies under LEO-relevant thermal-vacuum cycling and keV–MeV energetic ion irradiation. Performance degradation, failure modes, and robustness are assessed to inform the design and packaging of astrophotonic systems for space missions.

Items.Authors: Michał Kossakowski, Selina Ringsborg Howalt Owe, Rikke Stougaard Klausen, Alexander Cherlin, Denis Tcherniak, Alejandro Valverde Mahou, Søren Hauberg, Irfan Kuvvetli
Items.Title: Toward tracker-free Compton imaging: deep learning of charge cloud geometry in 3D CZT drift strip detectors
Items.Abstract: Recoil electron tracking is a key missing capability in Compton imaging for both high-sensitivity MeV gamma-ray astronomy and advanced medical imaging. This work presents a machine learning feasibility study investigating whether recoil electron direction and charge cloud geometry can be inferred directly from CZT detector pulse shapes. Synthetic data are generated using an Advanced Theoretical Detector Model of a 3D CZT Drift Strip Detector combined with recoil electron tracks simulated in GATE. The study defines the practical feasibility limits of AI-based electron tracking for next-generation Compton imaging systems.

Items.Authors: Alain Cournoyer, Hugo Bourque, Éric Carbonneau, Patrick Gilbert, Simon Houle, Jean-Alexis Boulet, Ian Silversides, Martin Larouche, Natalia Milaniak, Frédéric Grandmont, David Naylor, Brad Gom, Adam Christiansen, Matthew Buchan
Items.Title: TRL-5 cryogenic test campaign for the SAFARI scanning mirror mechanism design adopted for the phase delay mechanism of the PRIMA FIRESS instrument
Items.Abstract: We describe the Engineering Development Unit (EDU) of a novel cryogenic scanning mirror mechanism designed and built by ABB Inc. for SPICA and adopted for the Phase Delay Mechanism (PDM) of the Far-InfraRed Enhanced Survey Spectrometer (FIRESS) instrument on PRIMA. We report on TRL-5 demonstration results from the cryogenic EDU test campaign conducted by Blue Sky Spectroscopy Inc. (BSS) at the University of Lethbridge, verifying the compliance to the challenging SPICA and PRIMA requirements at 4 K (linear stroke, position and velocity stability, low heat dissipation, low magnetic emission, ultra-low photon leakage). The EDU was also integrated into a cryogenic far-infrared post-dispersed polarizing Fourier transform spectrometer designed and built by BSS and successfully tested at the University of Lethbridge to validate the scanning mechanism design.

Items.Authors: Jun Nishikawa, Naoshi Murakami, Kenta Yoneta, Yosuke Tanaka, Keigo Enya
Items.Title: Two-stage coronagraph for low scattered light and improved phase resolution control
Items.Abstract: We propose a two-stage coronagraph for high-contrast imaging. The first stage, a Lyot mask coronagraph, reflects the light for tip-tilt control and eliminates most of the light, minimizing scattered light generated by downstream optical elements. The second stage is a vortex phase mask coronagraph equipped with two deformable mirrors. The attenuated electric field from the first stage effectively improves the phase resolution of the deformable mirrors, enabling higher contrast control than conventional single-stage systems.

Items.Authors: Noelia Martínez Rey, Hajime Ogane, Joshua Carter, David Chandler, Jesse Cranney, Celine d'Orgeville, Dionne Haynes, Nicholas Herrald, Andrew W. Kruse, Lu Wang, Michitoshi Yoshida, Yosuke Minowa, Yusei Koyama, Junichi Katakura, Masayuki Akiyama, Hirofumi Okita, Yoshito H. Ono, Shin Oya, Naohisa Sato, Yuhei Takagi, Yoko Tanaka, Koki Terao, Chihiro Tokoku, Fumihiro Uraguchi, Yutaka Hayano, Masayuki Hirabayashi, Takamasa Bando, Masaki Morita, Shiang-Yu Wang, Chi-Yi Chou, Po-Chieh Yu
Items.Title: ULTIMATE-Subaru Ground Layer Adaptive Optics enters production phase at the Australian National University
Items.Abstract: The ULTIMATE GLAO system for the Subaru Telescope uses four side-launched laser guide stars to deliver wide-field image correction over a science field of 14x14 arcmin. Developed by Subaru in collaboration with NAOJ, Tohoku University, ASIAA, and ANU, ANU is leading the development of both the wavefront sensor (WFS) subsystem and the Laser Guide Star Facility (LGSF). The WFS includes four LGS and four NGS sensors to support the Wide-Field Imager planned for installation in 2028. In 2025 ANU completed prototypes of one LWFS, one NWFS, and a full-scale derotator assembly, within the WFS module, and the jitter correction subsystem in the LGSF. Both subsystems will enter production in 2026, and we present key prototyping outcomes and the planned production activities that will take place at ANU.

Items.Authors: Hirofumi Okita, Shin Oya, Yosuke Minowa, Yoshito Ono, Yuhei Takagi
Items.Title: ULTIMATE-Subaru: Interface between Adaptive Secondary Mirror and the Telescope
Items.Abstract: ULTIMATE-Subaru is an on-going project at the Subaru Telescope for the next-generation wide-field infrared astronomy with adaptive optics (AO). The adaptive secondary mirror (ASM) is one of the key components of the ULTIMATE-Subaru to provide improved seeing by ground-layer adaptive optics (GLAO). The ASM is carefully designed to replace the existing non-adaptive infrared secondary mirror (IR-M2) of the Subaru Telescope, with the minimum modification on the telescope and little impact on the existing instruments. The Top Unit Exchange (TUE) work, which has been conducted at the Subaru Telescope every two weeks on average to change the top unit(secondary mirrors or prime focus units/instruments), is the biggest difference from other 8-m class telescopes. The interface between the ASM and the telescope has been carefully considered to accommodate this TUE work. In this paper, we present the summary of the interface between the Subaru ASM and the telescope.

Items.Authors: Brody D. McElwain, Lakshmi Priya Keerthi Gurunathan, Brandon D. Chalifoux
Items.Title: Ultrafast laser stress figuring flat flex module prototypes
Items.Abstract: Building lightweight mirrors for X-ray telescopes is critical for future flagship-class NASA missions such as Lynx. Segmented X-ray mirror modules for such telescopes feature thin, tightly nested mirrors that are sensitive to coating and mounting processes. We have recently introduced Flex Modules, an X-ray mirror module design that allows for simultaneous figuring and aligning of X-ray mirror segments after coating and mounting. We have built flat Flex Module prototypes designed for testing simultaneous figuring and aligning of mirror areas using ultrafast laser stress figuring (ULSF), a non-contact figuring process that intentionally produces permanent and predictable stress in coated mirror substrates. In this paper we will focus on the ULSF process, including improvements made towards our finite element model for generating ULSF patterns. We present figuring and alignment results and show that ULSF has potential to meet requirements for future X-ray telescopes.

Items.Authors: Zhenyu Wu, Xin Huang, Yichen Liu, Tianxiang Chen, Yongquan Su, Na Gao, Xingwang Zhu, HuiLin He, Yupeng Xu
Items.Title: Ultrahigh-width-to-thickness ratio free-standing films for x-ray filter application
Items.Abstract: The Spectroscopy Focusing Array instrument, onboard the eXTP mission, will perform single-photon, high-resolution timing and energy measurements (0.5~10 keV) with a large collecting area. Since the UV, visible and infrared lights may cause thermal deformation of the operating instruments, which will decrease the detection accuracy, optical blocking filters are essential for optical blocking and thermal control purpose. This paper reports a free-standing filter with an ultra-high width-to-thickness ratio (WTR) of 1.5×105:1,which comprises a polyimide film as the mechanical support layer and Al as the optical functional layer, and is fabricated via Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) technology, enabling small-batch production. The filter has a visible light transmittance of 9.1×10-5 and maintains structural integrity under the simulated acoustic environment during satellite launch, which ensures the technical feasibility and reliability before and during the space X-ray detection.

Items.Authors: Luc Voruz, Alex Bayerle, Ramses Gunther, Christian Körnig, Adam Lassise, Bruno N. Menezes, Aditya Garde, Roland H. den Hartog, Henk Hoevers
Items.Title: Unlocking the potential of X-ray interferometry: manufacturing ultra-flat slatted mirrors with Silicon Pore Optics
Items.Abstract: X-ray interferometry has the potential to deliver unprecedented resolution. The design proposed by R. Willingale, which fits in a single spacecraft, relies on multi-layer slatted mirrors with stringent surface requirements. The SPO technology developed by cosine for ESA's NewAthena mission offers a great foundation for building such mirrors. SPO uses semiconductor-grade silicon wafers with extremely low surface roughness and thickness variation. They can be machined and cleaned with well-established processes, and bonded on top of each other.    In partnership with TU Delft and SRON, cosine has recently manufactured prototype slatted mirrors, leveraging SPO equipment and processes such as Laser MicroJet, SC-1 clean and ion beam figuring. The manufacturing process is fundamentally compatible with a future multi-layer version. This paper presents the status of the optics manufacturing and outlines the key technological steps needed to achieve the optics of the proposed XRIstel mission.

Items.Authors: Lorenzo Merli, Alessandro Ballone, Sylvain Cetre, David Barr, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Valentina Viotto, Luca Marafatto, Daniele Vassallo, Davide Greggio, Simone Di Filippo, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Jacopo Farinato, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Gabriele Umbriaco, Paolo Cerpelloni, Tania Gomes Machado
Items.Title: Update on the Control Pipeline for the MATTO test bench
Items.Abstract: MATTO is a wide field adaptive optics (AO) test bench currently under development at the INAF Astronomical Observatory of Padova. The facility is designed as a versatile platform for the study and validation of next-generation MCAO technologies.   Its architecture integrates several independently configurable optical and control elements, enabling the recreation of complex observing scenarios and a broad variety of conditions.  The scale and complexity of the bench place demanding requirements on its real-time control software. To meet these requirements, we are developing DAO4MATTO, a customized implementation of the Durham Adaptive Optics (DAO) real-time controller.  In this contribution, we report on the progress of the DAO4MATTO pipeline. After an overview of the MATTO concept, we describe recent work on hardware integration, data-flow design, and parallelization strategies. We also discuss implementation on a simplified bench configurations.

Items.Authors: Kyle Dalrymple, Aidan Gray, Mario Gennaro, Massimo Robberto, Stephen Smee, Stephen Hope, Robert Barkhouser, Randy Hammond
Items.Title: Updated results for optical properties of digital micromirror devices (DMDs) in the ultraviolet
Items.Abstract: Digital Micromirror Devices (DMDs), a class of micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS), are arrays of millions of ~10-micron-sized mirrors used for fine actuation and precise redirection of light. Development of this technology for astrophysical applications is relevant in the context of multi-object spectrographs (MOSs). We present calibration procedures as well as preliminary results of experiments to determine the scattering behavior of DMDs as they are swept through multiple wavelengths and angles of incidence. The impetus for DMD development is relevant, as the Astro2020 decadal survey calls for innovation relating to the development of multi-object spectrographs. DMDs are particularly useful for applications requiring multiple sightlines / multiple-object selection in crowded fields such as studies of the circum- and inter-galactic media, of accretion discs around young stellar objects, of massive stars and star clusters in the Local Volume, and more.

Items.Authors: Nemanja J. Jovanovic, Jeb I. Bailey, Takayuki Kotani, Gregory Sercel, Ashley D. Baker, Chris Betters, Andrew Ross-Adams, Sergio G. Leon-Saval, Rishi Pahuja, Jocelyn Ferrara, Jonathan Steiner, Truman Wold, Motohide Tamura
Items.Title: Updates on the full-scale development of the fiber delivery subsystem (FIB) of Keck/HISPEC
Items.Abstract: The High-Resolution Infrared Spectrometer for Exoplanet Characterization (HISPEC) will deliver R~100,000 spectroscopy from 0.98–2.5 μm at the Keck Observatory beginning in 2027. Its fiber delivery subsystem (FIB) routes adaptive-optics–corrected science and calibration light over 70 m using single-mode fibers (silica and custom ZBLAN) to deliver a stable, diffraction-limited line-spread function. A 3-port photonic lantern enhances efficiency in the y and J bands, while both mechanical and MEMS fiber switchers enable flexible light-path reconfiguration to route science light or a selection of diverse calibration sources achromatically over the two HISPEC bandpasses. FIB passed final design in 2024 and is now in full scale development. We summarize final test results, including the performance of the custom ZBLAN fiber, photonic lantern, MEMS switching tree, achromatic splitter, and low-loss mechanical switchers.

Items.Authors: Tânia Sofia Gomes Machado, Kalyan K. R. Santhakumari, Davide Greggio, Elisa Portaluri, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Alessandro Ballone, Federico Battaini, Maria Bergomi, Simone Di Filippo, Gianluca Di Rico, Marco Dima, Jacopo Farinato, Luigi Lessio, Demetrio Magrin, Luca Marafatto, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Valentina Viotto, Roberto Ragazzoni
Items.Title: Validating and characterising the Ingot WFS in a new ELT-like test bench
Items.Abstract: The Ingot Wavefront Sensor (I-WFS) offers a novel strategy to optimize wavefront sensing with Laser Guide Stars (LGS) for Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs) using a side laser launcher. Unlike classical WFSs, the Ingot design is specifically thought to address the challenges posed by the extended geometry of the LGS. We present results from the Ingot WFS's latest in-lab demonstration, conducted on a redesigned test bench that accurately replicates key ELT parameters. The setup includes an LGS-like source that incorporates real sodium concentration profiles and solves pupil gradient issues previously encountered. The inclusion of an ALPAO DM292 Deformable Mirror in the design enables the critical study of the WFS response to high-order aberrations. We detail the main characteristics of this bench and the next steps in order to study the I-WFS sensitivity, linearity, and quasi closed-loop performance.

Items.Authors: Yasumasa Yamasaki, Satoru Iguchi
Items.Title: Verification of quantization efficiency and linearity of input-output response in digitizing for radio astronomical observations
Items.Abstract: An astronomical signal can be addressed as a normal random number that follows a Gaussian distribution of its amplitude. The signal is finally sampled, quantized and digitized before spectroscopic or correlation processing at radio telescope. The quantization efficiency is maximized by adjusting the input power to digitizer. The input power to digitizer has been designed to be within the range where the quantization efficiencies meet the sensitivity requirement in radio astronomical observations. However, we must consider not only the sensitivity maximum but also the accuracy or distortion of waves in digitizing. In this paper, we will report the verification tests about the quantization efficiency and the linearity of the input-output response in digitizing. To meet the high precise observation requirement, the digitizer’s input power should be designed to be much lower than the input power at the highest quantization efficiency by taking into consideration the linearity response.

Items.Authors: Sirinrat Sithajan, Surangkhana Rukdee, Pakakaew Rittipruk, Lalita Kaewbiang
Items.Title: VIOLA exposure-time calculator
Items.Abstract: The VIPA-based Instrument for an Oxygen-Loaded Atmosphere (VIOLA) is a high-throughput, ultra-high-resolution near-infrared spectrograph (R ≈ 300,000) covering the J and H bands, enabling simultaneous detection of molecular oxygen (O₂) and methane (CH₄), key biosignature gases in exoplanet atmospheres. To support design optimization, performance evaluation, and future operations, we developed the VIOLA Exposure-Time Calculator (ETC), a Python-based tool with a web-based Streamlit interface that predicts the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and estimates the detection significance of molecular features under user-defined observing conditions by modeling the photon budget from source to detector, including throughput, telluric transmission, and background noise. The ETC uses a modular architecture that separates instrument, observing-condition, and target components, allowing straightforward updates and integration into VIOLA observation planning.

Items.Authors: Daniel Lancaster, Stefan Kraus, Owain Snaith, Sorabh Chhabra, Jyotirmay Paul, Michael Ireland, Narsireddy Anugu, John Monnier
Items.Title: Visibility characterisation and reduction of the BIFROST instrument
Items.Abstract: BIFROST is soon to be part of the ASGARD visitor suite of instruments for the  Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI). BIFROST will have two spectrographs that can be used together for fringe tracking and for different spectral resolutions. One of the most important measurements for an interferometer is the visibility. Instrumentation effects which result in uncertainties or systematic errors in the visibility must, therefore, be characterised. This report aims to address the issue by identifying sources of vibration and other visibility causing effects within BIFROST and also the wider instrument as a whole. This will identify the main limiting factors and mitigating measures that can be taken in the future including stability and pipeline work that will be needed.

Items.Authors: Ross Robinson, Zoran Ninkov, Wyatt Robinson, Kevin Kearney
Items.Title: VIS-VUV radiometric calibration facility for space-based instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Rapid develop cycles enable SmallSat platforms to achieve low-cost1 UV access compared to the extended development timelines of flagship missions. However, radiometric verification of optics, coatings, filters and detector QE is still needed for mission success. This testing needs to be done efficiently with both schedule and cost to not compromise the SmallSat advantages.       The Laboratory for Advanced Instrumentation Research (LAIR) at Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) is developing a radiometric calibration facility to compress instrument-level test timelines for emerging SmallSat UV programs. The facility supports characterization of astrophysical instrumentation as well as development of sensors and optics for defense and semiconductor manufacturing. The current configuration is a dual monochromator system for 120nm - 1100nm coverage.

Items.Authors: Kevin W. Fogarty, Rachel E. Morgan, Ruslan Belikov, Eduardo A. Bendek, Jonathan Lin, Dan Sirbu
Items.Title: Wavefront control for experimental verification of simulated contrast performance for the AstroPIC photonic coronagraph
Items.Abstract: Photonic coronagraphy has the potential to dramatically improve our ability to target faint, small-separation exoplanets with future missions such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory. A practical photonic integrated circuit (PIC) coronagraph will need to be able to create a dark zone in multiple output channels (in order to provide spatial and potentially spectral information about detected exoplanets) and have finite spectral bandwidth. We have previously shown in simulation that a PIC with a relatively small number of input and output channels is capable of creating a ~ 2% spectral band with 1e-10 contrast in a single output channel, and is capable of creating a monochromatic dark zone in multiple output channels simultaneously in the presence of realistic directional coupler biases. Simulation work was performed assuming a 9-input, 9-output triangular mesh PIC, which corresponds to the AstroPIC Cycle 1 laboratory experiment. We follow up on these results by modelling processes observed in the lab with AstroPIC, and using this model to develop wavefront control for upcoming verification experiments with AstroPIC. We adapt the optimization routine used in simulation for upcoming lab experiments and demonstrate digging a broadband dark zone with limited model knowledge of the AstroPIC chip. We report on the performance of photonic coronagraphs across axes of bandwidth, number of channels, and number of modes suppressed with ideal model knowledge, and compare with wavefront control using limited model knowledge. We discuss plans for implementation of lab demonstrations for broadband and multi-channel dark zones with hardware currently being installed.

Items.Authors: Sheng-Feng Lin
Items.Title: Wide-angle 3× inner-zoom and inner-focus lens design using all-spherical elements for spaceborne imaging instrumentations
Items.Abstract: Spaceborne imaging systems require robust optical architectures capable of maintaining stable image quality across varying focal lengths while operating under extreme environmental conditions. This paper presents the design of a five-group wide-angle optical system incorporating an inner 3× zoom and inner focusing lens groups with stationary total track length within 350mm, implemented exclusively with spherical lens elements. By eliminating the use of aspherical surfaces, the proposed design enhances manufacturability, alignment stability, and radiation robustness for long-duration space missions. The optical configuration consists of a retrofocus front group, an internal zoom variator, a fixed aperture stop to suppress focus breathing effects, an inner focusing compensator, and a rear image-forming group. Aberration correction is achieved through optimized optical power distribution, glass material selection, and element splitting strategies.

Items.Authors: Arend Moerman, Akira Endo, Stefanie Brackenhoff, Shinji Fujita, Shiro Ikeda, Kenichi Karatsu, Kotaro Kohno, Yuri Nishimura, Matus Rybak, Tatsuya Takekoshi, Yoichi Tamura, Akio Taniguchi, Javier Aguilera, Hiroki Akamatsu, Tom Bakx, Bruno Buijtendorp, Scott Cray, Shahab Dabironezare, Yasunori Fujii, Sho Fujisawa, Kazuyuki Fujita, Masato Hagimoto, Shaul Hanany, Shunsuke Honda, Shuji Hotta, Robert Huiting, Takahiro Iino, Chihiro Imamura, Shuhei Inoue, Akira Inoue, Shutaro Inui, Shun Ishii, Yuji Ishizaki, Kotaro Iwakami, Masato Kato, Ryohei Kawabe, Nick de Keijzer, Tetsu Kitayama, Micah Klettke, Toshihiko Kobiki, Ryoya Kojima, Kuniaki Konishi, Ryusuke Koriyama, Hosun Lee, Fumiya Maeda, Louis Marting, Tomotake Matsumura, Ren Matsusaka, Tetsuhiro Minamidani, Kana Morokuma, Vignesh Murugesan, Maki Nagata, Shunichi Nakatsubo, Kanako Narita, Rallou Nikolopoulou, Kazushige Ohtawara, Norika Okauchi, Leon Olde Scholtenhuis, Tai Oshima, Alejandro Pascual Laguna, Madelief Peters, Lucie Rowland, Seiichi Sakamoto, Haruyuki Sakurai, Masaki Sakakibara, Yuma Sato, Mizuki Sato, Mahoshi Sawamura, Fenno Steenvoorde, Ryota Takaku, David Thoen, Huckleberry Thums, Akiyoshi Tsujita, Hideki Umehata, Shinsuke Uno, Sten Vollebregt, Kazuki Watanabe, Paul van der Werf, Doreen Wernicke, Beth Westoby, Juri Yamanaka, Stephen Yates, Jochem Baselmans
Items.Title: Wideband (sub)millimeter observations of the galaxy cluster RX J1347.5-1145 with DESHIMA 2.0
Items.Abstract: We report on wideband (sub)millimeter observations of the galaxy cluster RX J1347.5-1145 with the DESHIMA 2.0 instrument, during its commissioning and science verification campaign at the ASTE 10-meter telescope in 2024. DESHIMA 2.0 is an on-chip spectrometer, operating between 200-400 GHz with a moderate filterbank resolution of R ~ 500 which targets the SZ effect of the galaxy cluster. In order to spatially scan the cluster, a special on-the-fly (OTF) mapping strategy was used.  We present the OTF mapping strategy that was used, the data reduction pipeline and mapmaking, and the current efforts and state of analysis of the galaxy cluster data. We will also present results of the pipeline applied to blank sky data in order to verify the quality of the pipeline and to demonstrate photon-noise-limited performance. Finally, we will give an outlook on the scientific analysis that can be performed on the galaxy cluster data.

Items.Authors: Simone D'Auria, Andrea Tozzi, Matteo Munari, Anna Brucalassi, Sofia Randich, Alen Khanbekyan, Roland Bacon, David Lee
Items.Title: WST, the wide-field spectroscopic telescope: mechanical design and FE analysis for the high-resolution spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST) is a planned 12 m-class spectroscopic facility for large surveys. This paper reports on Work Package 4.5, focused on the High-Resolution Multi-Object Spectrograph (MOS-HR). The instrument will provide R = 40,000 with 2,000 targets. We describe the mechanical design activities defining the opto-mechanical architecture. To satisfy scientific requirements and manufacturability constraints, the layout is organized into four modules, each with two sub-modules adopting a vertical optical-bench configuration with elements mounted on both sides. From the baseline optical design, the mechanical configuration was developed to ensure alignment accuracy, structural stability, and environmental robustness. The workflow includes translation of the optical prescription into a mechanical model, definition of mounting and alignment interfaces, and preliminary static, modal, and seismic analyses. The output is the estimation of mass, volume, costs and others.

Items.Authors: Matteo Munari, Andrea Tozzi, Anna Brucalassi
Items.Title: WST, the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope: the preliminary optical design for the MOS-HR spectrograph
Items.Abstract: In the frame of the study for WST, the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope, a 12 meter class telescope completly devoted to spectroscopic surveys, the realization of a High-Resolution Multi Object Spectrograph (MOS-HR) has been proposed. We present here the main characteristics of the optical design of the spectrograph, describing the requirements, the adopted solutions and the foreseen permances, with an eye on future trade-offs.

Items.Authors: Massinissa Hadjara, Teng Xu, Yue Sun, Wei Wei, Chao Liu, Hang Zhang, Junzhe Huang, Changyu Zeng, Jianqing Yuan, Jérémy Perdigon, Abdelkarim Boskri, Stéphane Lagarde, Romain Petrov, Roxanne Ligi, Bruno Lopez, Florentin Millour, Julien Dejonghe, Fabien Baron
Items.Title: XuYi’s interferometer observation simulator
Items.Abstract: We present a unified simulation tool for the XuYi optical interferometer, designed to evaluate the observability, (u,v)-coverage, delay-line evolution, visibilities, and spectra of selected stars from the XuYi Mountain site. The simulator, implemented in MATLAB, uses the three-telescope configuration (baselines of 55–100 m) and includes the 44 m delay-line limitation. It provides observability diagrams incorporating Sun/Moon constraints and airmass, as well as (u,v)-coverage with configurable temporal sampling. Interferometric visibilities are computed using angular diameters from several diameter catalogues, with both Uniform Disk and Limb-Darkened models. When available, stellar spectra (H band and others) are included. The tool also generates synthetic interferometric observables based on physical models such as SCIROCCO and PAMPERO, exportable in OIFITS format. This simulator offers an efficient platform for planning and optimizing future interferometric observations at XuYi.

Items.Authors: Florian Gollier, Esther del Pino Rosendo, Tony B. Hull, Janina Krieg, Antoine Carré, Thomas Westerhoff
Items.Title: ZERODUR®’s characteristics enable large extremely-stable spaceborne mirrors
Items.Abstract: ZERODUR® is now in its successful 6th decade of continuously controlled production, and the non-proprietary history of these mirrors in space has been published. Over 13 years ago, SCHOTT presented in a conference exhibit, a highly lightweighted 1.2m diameter specimen mirror, 88% lightweighted with a first eigenfrequency of 212Hz. Extreme lightweighting of large ZERODUR® mirrors is available from SCHOTT, augmented by a dedicated 5,000 m2 facility with state-of-the-art environmental controls and machines. In this facility, mirror substrates greater than 4 meters in diameter are produced. ZERODUR®'s material strength has been exhaustively studied, yielding extensive Weibull Statistics consistent with large spaceborne mirrors of other materials. Evidence-based design is possible with SCHOTT's full publication of latest material data on strength, thermal characteristics and environmental resilience plus statistics of 949 1.5-m diameter ZERODUR® mirror blanks for ELT.

Items.Authors: Mattéo Pasinetti, Benoît Neichel, Andrew Reeves, Perrine Lognoné, Morgan Gray, Nicolas Védrenne, Cyril Petit, Pierre Louis Mayeur, Thierry Fusco, Francisco Oyarzun, Esteban Vera, Benjamín Andres González Barraza, Rodrigo Andres Muñoz Gomez, Sylvain Cetre
Items.Title: AO4FEELINGS: a new versatile adaptive optics testbench for advanced control in satellite communications and wide-field astronomy
Items.Abstract: We introduce AO4FEELINGS, a new versatile Adaptive Optics testbench developed for the FEELINGS telescope, an ONERA facility capable of tracking LEO and GEO satellites. Resulting from a collaboration between LAM, ONERA, Durham University, and PUCV, this platform bridges the gap between simulation and on-sky validation. The work presented here focuses on the bench commissioning and the first experimental results of the comparative analysis of downlink control strategies, including classical integrators, Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control, and Reinforcement Learning (RL). The testbench is also designed to serve as a future testbed for phase prediction algorithms at the Point-Ahead Angle (PAA). Validating these predictive strategies in an uplink-like scenario will provide valuable insights for both FSOC and wide-field astronomical applications.

Items.Authors: Markus Wittkowski, Giacomo Beccari, Akke Corporaal, Abigail Frost, Olivier Hainaut, Xavier Haubois, Jens Kammerer, Aaron Labdon, Antoine Mérand, Johan Olofsson, Anna Francesca Pala, Claudia Paladini, Isabelle Percheron, Monika Petr-Gotzens, John Pritchard, Marina Rejkuba, Miguel Vioque, Julien Woillez
Items.Title: ESO User Support and Observation Preparation for VLTI Operations
Items.Abstract: We present recent enhancements to VLTI observing capabilities from a user-oriented perspective, together with new  developments in ESO’s Observation Handling Tools and end-to-end operations model for VLTI. Key upgrades include  GRAVITY+ Coudé guiding with laser guide stars at the UTs, and improved limiting magnitudes for GRAVITY and  MATISSE, all supported by a streamlined, uniform template structure. Phase 2 tools now enable finding-chart generation and the selection of Coudé guide stars and fringe-tracker targets, and will soon offer expanded preparation features. We summarise usage statistics for snapshot, astrometric, imaging, and time-series observations, outline VLTI scheduling considerations, and present new video tutorials. Starting in 2026, an archive data stream of reduced GRAVITY dispersed visibilities has become available. Complementary community engagement in VLTI operations continues to grow. We close by identifying operational lessons for future interferometric facilities.

Items.Authors: Daan Roos, Shahab Dabironezare, Stephen Yates, Daniela Perez Capelo, Hendrik Veen, Dimitry Lamers, David Thoen, Jochem Baselmans, Stafford Withington, Willem Jellema
Items.Title: Multi-mode characterisation of a 1.5 THz lens-absorber coupled kinetic inductance detector via energy absorption interferometry
Items.Abstract: Future far-infrared missions such as PRIMA require detectors with background-limited sensitivity and strong optical coupling. Lens-absorber KIDs are promising for super-THz frequencies because their incoherent response is robust to fabrication tolerances, but they are sensitive to multiple spatial modes that can degrade system performance. To investigate this behaviour, we analysed a 1.5 THz lens-absorber KID using Energy Absorption Interferometry and a complementary spectral model. EAI illuminates the detector using two phase-controlled sources to recover the detector’s spatial coherence. The simulated modes, propagated through the optical system, showed excellent agreement with experimental measurements. This validates EAI as a reliable way to assess the impact of lens-absorber design on its modal response, and better instrument design for upcoming far-infrared imagers.

Items.Authors: Sebastian J. Diebold, Desiree Ferreira, Michael J. Freyberg, Bastian Heß, Sonny Massahi, Diego Paredes-Sanz, Emanuele Perinati, Finn Pfeifle, Andrea Santangelo, Lothar Schmidt, Beate Stelzer, Sara Svendsen, Chris Tenzer, Tim Wildfang
Items.Title: Soft proton experiments supporting the development of astronomical X-ray instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Orbital soft protons can seriously degrade the instrumental performance of astronomical X-ray observatories. On the one hand, they pose the risk to damage X-ray sensors permanently, and, on the other hand, they introduce a non-reducible background component.    With our low-energy grazing-angle scattering setup we provide experimental input and validation for radiation transport simulations that are used for the assessment of future X-ray missions. Our latest experimental results point out that a majority of protons scattered on X-ray optics undergoes charge exchange and, thus, cannot be mitigated by magnetic diverters. Furthermore, we investigated energy loss and charge exchange fractions in thin filters typically used in X-ray instruments and compared the results to simulations with TRIM and Geant4.    In this contribution, we present our upgraded experimental setup as well as our latest results on grazing-angle scattering and foil transmission measurements.

Items.Authors: Pietro Schipani, Sergio Campana, Paolo D'Avanzo, Riccardo U. Claudi, Matteo Aliverti, Giulio Capasso, Mirko Colapietro, Francesco D'Alessio, Matteo Genoni, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Marco Landoni, Matteo Munari, Frédéric Dérie, Markus Schoeller, Emanuela Pompei, Davide Ricci, Salvatore Scuderi, Fabrizio Vitali, Rosario Cosentino, Federico Battaini, Simone Di Filippo, Andrea Baruffolo, Sagi Ben-Ami, David Young, Anna Brucalassi, Stephen Smartt, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Giuliano Pignata, Lorenzo Cabona, Enrico Cappellaro, Massimo Della Valle, Sergio D'Orsi, Luigi Lessio, Laurent Marty, Bernardo Salasnich, Salvatore Savarese, Ricardo Zanmar Sánchez, Marco Riva, Jose Antonio Araiza-Durán, Matteo Accardo, Geza Csoernyei, Derek Ives, Hans-Ulrich Kaufl, Leander Mehrgan, Andrea Modigliani, Luca Pasquini, Ivo Saviane, Armin Silber, Simone Doniselli, Silvio De Rosa, Antonio Sulich, Ofir Hershko, Alex Bichkovsky, Adam Rubin, Michael Rappaport, Avishay Gal-Yam, Hector Ventura, Marcos Hernandez, Iair Arcavi, Seppo Mattila, Maximilian Stritzinger
Items.Title: SOXS at the NTT: completion and first on-sky performance of the new transient spectroscopic facility
Items.Abstract: The Son Of X-Shooter (SOXS) instrument equips ESO’s NTT with broad-band spectroscopy optimized for time-domain and transient astronomy. Covering 0.35–2.0 μm with two simultaneous spectrographic arms and an acquisition/imaging channel, SOXS delivers efficient target acquisition, wide spectral coverage, and high throughput for all kinds of transients. The project completed the AIV phase in Italy, achieved Preliminary Acceptance in Europe, and was then shipped to Chile for reassembly, alignment, and full verification at La Silla. On-site work included telescope interfacing, system debugging, and validation of the instrument software and pipeline using on-sky data. First-light observations show that SOXS meets or exceeds its design spectral-resolution goals, and early verification data demonstrate its capability to obtain rapid, high-quality spectra across the full wavelength range. The paper summarizes these activities, lessons learned, and representative commissioning results.

Items.Authors: Matthew V. Radovan, Max Baeten, Mike Dahler, Bert Dekker, Luke Gers, Phil Hinz, Royce Jarrad, Marc Kassis, Stefan S. Kuiper, Martin Lemmen, David Limbert, Emily Plume, Christopher Ratliff, Ed Wetherell
Items.Title: The Keck Adaptive Secondary Mirror: a new prime focus capability for the Keck I Telescope
Items.Abstract: UCO is leading the development of a 1.5-meter-diameter Keck Adaptive Secondary Mirror (KASM) that will use approximately 3000 Hybrid Variable Reluctance (HVR) actuators developed by TNO (Netherlands Organization for Applied Research). KASM will provide ground-layer AO correction and improved throughput for the suite of instruments on the Keck I telescope. Focus and tip-tilt correction for KASM will be managed by a hexapod attached to a Top End Module (TEM) repurposed from the decommissioned F/25 secondary mirror.  This paper describes the challenges of improving the 35-year-old Keck I telescope by installing an adaptive secondary mirror at a focal station that hasn’t seen a new instrument in over 2 decades. We discuss important details and challenges related to the mechanical, optical, and thermal interfaces, all of which are critical to KASM's success.

Items.Authors: Damien Galano, Raphael Rougeot, Jorg Versluys, Teodor Bozhanov, Jonathan Grzymisch, Joe Zender, Esther Bastida Pertegaz, Miho Janvier, Yann Scoarnec, Daniel Serrano, Sergio Tiraplegui, Juan Antonio Béjar, Julien Peyrard, Lorenzo Montagna, Jean-Francois Hamel, Pamela Woo, Mike Margreve, Mathias Benn, John Leif Jorgensen, Davide Loreggia, Gerardo Capobianco, Alessandro Bemporad, Silvano Fineschi, Marta Casti, Cedric Thizy, Andrei Zhukov
Items.Title: ESA Proba-3 formation flying performance enabling low straylight Sun corona observations
Items.Abstract: The ESA Proba-3 mission is a groundbreaking project to demonstrate and validate the concept of precise formation flying, with millimetric accuracy. It involves two spacecraft flying 150 meters apart and together forming a giant solar coronagraph. Following their launch in December 2024, the Proba-3 spacecraft entered routine science operations in July 2025.  This paper presents the achieved formation flying performance of the Proba-3 spacecraft relevant for the coronagraphic observations, gathered from the satellites’ in-flight data. Moreover it describes how the formation flying enables the observation of the poorly explored inner region of the sun corona by minimizing the straylight level. Finally it discusses the main factors influencing the formation flying performance, including the on-board sensors accuracy, the satellites’ specific orbit and the capabilities of the propulsion system.

Items.Authors: Gavin S. Hay, Mark Barnet, Scott Christie, Saugata Dutt, Suresh Sivanandam
Items.Title: Development of a high-reliability planetary gearbox for cryogenic ultra-high vacuum applications
Items.Abstract: GIRMOS is a near-infrared, multi-object, medium spectral resolution, integral field spectrograph in development for the Gemini North Observatory, containing 15 cryogenic mechanisms that must operate reliably for 10–15 years. The baselined commercial cryogenic motor–gearbox units raised concerns over long-term reliability due to unlubricated CRES 440C bearings prone to cold welding and WS₂-lubricated gears susceptible to fatigue failure. Cryogenic life testing of a prototype mechanism confirmed these issues when the gearbox failed early after only 60 cycles. Dunlap Engineering developed a drop-in replacement gearbox using three CRES 15-5PH planetary stages dry-lubricated with MoS₂, with geometry optimized for dry lubricant life. A hybrid main bearing (440C races, SiC balls, WS₂), Vespel SP-3 bumpers, and a new motor with WS₂-lubricated hybrid ceramic bearings complete the design. All parts are in manufacture, and life testing of the first unit is expected soon after.

Items.Authors: Benjamin L. Gerard, Dominic Sanchez, Aditya R. Sengupta, Christopher Ratliff, Sylvain Scetre, Elinor Gates, Daren Dillon, Bautista Fernandez, Brian Bauman, Lisa Poyneer, Aaron Lemmer, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Phillip M. Hinz, Bruce Macintosh
Items.Title: On-sky results from REDWOODS, a platform at Lick/ShaneAO for testing second stage AO technologies
Items.Abstract: Adaptive optics (AO) and high contrast exoplanet imaging technology development is a key priority set forth by the 2020 Decadal Survey of Astronomy and Astrophysics to bridge the 100x contrast gap needed for near infrared habitable exoplanet imaging with future Extremely Large Telescopes. REDWOODS—Real time Exoplanet Direct imaging via Wavefront control Of Optical DefectS—is a collaboration between Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) and University of California Santa Cruz (UCSC) designed to test AO technologies to bridge this gap with upgrades to the Shane AO system at Lick Observatory. We present (1) the opto-mechanical design, (2) integration at testing both before and after installation at the Shane telescope, and (3) on-sky results.   This work was performed under the auspices of the U.S. Department of Energy by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory under Contract DE-AC52-07NA27344. This document number is LLNL-ABS-2013819.

Items.Authors: Bianca Salmaso, Stefano Basso, Davide Sisana, Akanshu Chauhan, Simone Marini, Benedetta Dalla Barba, Adam Rizkallah, Mauro Ghigo, Daniele Spiga, Gabriele Vecchi, Giorgia Sironi, Giovanni Pareschi, Gianpiero Tagliaferri, Michela C. A. Uslenghi, Mauro Fiorini, Luigi Lessio, Simonetta Chinellato, Claudio Ferrari, Elena Ferrari, Vadim Burwitz, Marcos Bavdaz, Ivo Ferreira
Items.Title: Advancing BEaTriX for enhanced x-ray calibrations
Items.Abstract: The Beam Expander Testing X-ray facility (BEaTriX), operated at the Brera Observatory of the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), is a cutting-edge calibration facility for testing Silicon Pore Optics Mirror Modules (SPO MM) for the ESA’s NewAthena mission. It currently supports calibration at the energy of 4.51 keV, with the first operational beam line successfully in use since 2022. The second X-ray source and beam conditioning optics are now under realization to expand the calibration capabilities to the energy of 1.49 keV. Additionally, efforts are being made to extend its flexibility by modifying the focal length from a fixed NewAthena-dedicated setup to a tunable range between 1.4 and 14 meters. This paper presents recent advancements in these developments and highlights key technical progress for enhancing BEaTriX's operational versatility.

Items.Authors: Roberta Pellegrini, Piero Gregori, Francesco Maria Cerutti, Tharek Mohtar, Francesco Diprima, Elena Vellutini
Items.Title: Development of the Flyeye shutter for SST application from tracklet acquisition to characterization: high temporal accuracy for optimized orbit determination performance
Items.Abstract: The Flyeye Telescope (FET) for Space Surveillance and Tracking, built by OHB Italia for ASI, is the first set of four telescopes in a planned global network aimed to detect and catalog space debris and other objects.  Unlike earlier Flyeye models, it is optimized for demanding SST tasks. Its key innovation is a custom dual-blade shutter accurately synchronized with the CCD camera, enabling accurate tracklet acquisition. A dedicated calibration mode determines CCD column positions and blade alignment.  The system’s strength is its accurate timing, linked to GPS, achieving 133 µs RMS accuracy to meet the 0.4-arcsec astrometric requirement allowing the orbit determination of fast-moving satellites.  During each exposure, the shutter performs two asymmetric open/close cycles, producing paired tracklets that reveal both angular velocity and object direction. Combined with star-field calibration, these measurements can be used for accurate initial orbit determination and orbit refinement.

Items.Authors: Anaïs Besnard, Valentin Sauvage, Giulia Connena, Kenichi Karatsu, Stephen Yates, Lorenza Ferrari, Bruno Maffei
Items.Title: New method for cosmic ray hits deglitching
Items.Abstract: Aiming to characterize the susceptibility of new generations of highly sensitive cryogenic detector to high energy particles such as cosmic rays, IAS has developed a cryogenic test facility which can operate detectors or parts of focal planes at temperatures ranging from 50 to 300 mK while performing particle irradiations. Coupling this facility to a particle accelerator beam allows for impact studies through single event spurious signal on the data (glitches), and total irradiation dose to simulate several years of operation in space causing potential performance degradations. The glitch shape analysis, giving access to the detector time constants, leads to the possibility of establishing a thermal model but also to the possibility of glitch removal in the data through a new deglitching method that has been developed.

Items.Authors: Joel Sanchez-Bermudez
Items.Title: Deep Image Prior Neural Networks for interferometric image reconstruction
Items.Abstract: We present an interferometric image-reconstruction framework based on Deep Image Prior (DIP) auto-encoders to recover high-angular-resolution images from sparse Fourier data without supervised training. An untrained U-Net-like network is optimized per dataset through a non-uniform Fourier forward model acting on visibility (squared) amplitudes and closure phases, while explicit regularizers (e.g. total variation, flux, compactness and centroid terms) encode physical constraints. We show the performance of this technology on observations taken with different facilities: JWST Sparse Aperture Masking data, the Event Horizon Telescope and the Very Large Telescope interferometer GRAVITY instrument. We highlight in this work how this approach provides a unified, instrument-agnostic pathway for next-generation interferometric imaging based on unsupervised deep priors.

Items.Authors: Kevin W. Sacca, Matt Beasley, Craig DeForest, Ronnie Killough, Glenn Laurent, Nicholas Erickson, Travis Smith, Reith Nolan, Todd Veach, Robert Klar, Marcus Hughes
Items.Title: Overview and status of the Space-weather Solar Coronagraph (SwSCOR) instruments
Items.Abstract: The Space-weather Solar Coronagraph (SwSCOR) instruments are in development to provide the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Space weather Observations at Lagrange 1 (L1) for Advanced Readiness (SOLAR) program with continuity and resilience of solar wind data and coronal mass ejection (CME) imagery. The SwSCOR project, led by Southwest Research Institute (SwRI), consists of a coronagraph instrument and a set of ground processing algorithms designed to produce space weather imagery. The instrument is a single-stage, externally occulted coronagraph and the camera and electronics are adapted and tailored for the SwSCOR project from versions already developed for NASA’s Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) Small Explorer mission. SwSCOR is intended to deliver real-time, forecast-quality images of the solar K corona (sunlight scattered by free electrons near the Sun), allowing forecasters to characterize and track space weather as it leaves the Sun.

Items.Authors: Maaike A. M. van Kooten, Kate Jackson, Jean-Pierre Veran, Olivier Lardiere, Jenny Atwood
Items.Title: REVOLT 3.0: redesign towards visible and LGS AO
Items.Abstract: The NRC-Herzberg Adaptive Optics (AO) team has completed a design study to upgrade the REVOLT AO system, extending its capabilities into the visible regime by implementing Laser Guide Star (LGS) operations. The upgrade enhances the system’s performance for science requiring diffraction-limited imaging at shorter wavelengths.   We investigated the option of placing a UV laser on an independent platform to allow elongation experiments, enabling REVOLT to serve as a flexible testbed for LGS-related studies. In parallel, we assessed the integration of an Adaptive Secondary Mirror on the telescope to improve optical throughput. Beyond REVOLT's role as a technology demonstrator, we plan to open REVOLT for limited community science access. This upgrade strengthens NRC-Herzberg’s leadership in AO development, enables new capabilities to observers, provides training for next generation of AO scientists, and lays the groundwork for future AO systems on next-generation telescopes.

Items.Authors: Patrick J. Ingraham, Jaegun Yoo, Phil Stahl, Ewan Douglas, Daewook Kim
Items.Title: Thermal vacuum characterization of a spin-cast, Honeycomb Structured Borosilicate Mirror
Items.Abstract: Borosilicate mirrors are commonplace in ground-based observatories but their potential for space-based applications is now gathering attention. One significant challenge is the relatively high coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) making their figure sensitive to thermal gradients. Pushing to colder operational temperatures to minimize thermal background radiation is also desired, potentially inducing surface errors from CTE variations. To better characterize the thermal properties of these mirrors, a “thin” 7-core honeycomb mirror was cast and figured at the University of Arizona’s Richard F. Caris Mirror Lab. In a collaboration with NASA's X-Ray Cryogenic Facility, the surface figure was measured at temperatures ranging from 293K to 37K. This paper presents the initial results and their implication on operational temperature ranges for this class of mirror. It also discusses how the results impact the development of temperature control systems for future space missions.

Items.Authors: John I. Bailey, Jason Fucik, Richard Dekany, Reston B. Nash, Jocelyn Ferrara, Christoffer Fremling, Roger Smith, Dan Reiley, Yashvi Sharma, Prakriti Gupta, Robert Weber, Don Neill, Mansi M. Kasliwal, Shrinivas R. Kulkarni
Items.Title: ZShooter for Keck I: an AO‑ready 310-2450 nm echelle spectrograph with a tri‑band millisecond imager
Items.Abstract: ZShooter is a proposed always‑online facility instrument for Keck I that combines ZSpec, a three‑arm 310--2450 nm echelle spectrograph, with ZImager, a co‑aligned three‑channel millisecond imager. This work describes the overall system architecture, ZSpec and ZImager optical designs, and the role of low‑noise qCCD and APD detectors in enabling performance. We will highlight science cases in time‑domain and stellar astrophysics, discuss design studies of systematic noise when re‑binning high‑resolution spectra to low resolving power for classification, and cover our an integrated instrument‑control and data‑pipeline framework.

Items.Authors: Yilong Zhang
Items.Title: Terahertz astronomical interferometry project at Antarctic Dome A
Items.Abstract: The terahertz band is a crucial electromagnetic window for studying galaxy formation and evolution, planetary origins, and cosmic microwave background radiation, and it plays an increasingly vital role in cutting-edge astronomical research. Dome A in Antarctica is a globally unique and superior ground-based site for terahertz astronomical observation. Taking these exceptional advantages, the research team from the Purple Mountain Observatory is conducting a terahertz astronomical interferometry project at Antarctic Dome. The project's scientific objective is to conduct high-resolution interferometric observations to obtain direct measurements of the black hole dust torus and the starburst activity in its host galaxy. This work is expected to yield breakthrough insights into the structure of the dust torus and its larger-scale galactic environment. We will report on the current development progress of the 1-meter terahertz telescope.

Items.Authors: Anthony I. Huber, Jason Austermann, James Beall, James Burgoyne, Scott Chapman, Douglas Henke, Johannes Hubmayr, Matthew Koc, Jeffrey van Lanen, Adrian Sinclair, Anna Vaskuri, Michael Vissers, Jordan Wheeler, Ruixuan Xie
Items.Title: CCAT: characterization of the first KID array for the Prime-Cam 850 GHz module
Items.Abstract: The Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST) is a 6-meter crossed-Dragone telescope developed by the CCAT collaboration. Sited at 5600 m, FYST will provide superior observing conditions for submillimeter astronomy. Prime-Cam is a first-generation instrument designed to house multiple separate camera modules. The 850 GHz module of Prime-Cam is the highest-frequency band and is designed to deploy ~38,000 polarization-sensitive lumped-element kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs) across 3 arrays. These detectors incorporate a novel two-octave resonator network design to maximize multiplexing in an RFSoC readout system. We review the design and fabrication process for the 850 GHz KIDs. We present the characterization of the first KID array developed for the 850 GHz module, including optical and dark testing, and noise performance. We discuss the measured optical efficiency, sensitivity, and uniformity and the expected on-sky performance. The 850 GHz module will be deployed in 2017.

Items.Authors: Will Saunders, Corentin Cudennec, Roland Bacon, Philippe Dierickx, Roelof de Jong, David Lee, Gaston Gausachs
Items.Title: Design evolution for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope
Items.Abstract: WST combines MOS and IFS modes, each at an order-of-magnitude greater scale than current systems, presenting unprecedented design challenges.  For MOS, both science and spectrograph considerations demand excellent delivered image quality, notwithstanding the huge etendue (12m aperture, 2 degree field). Eventually, 3-lens forward-Cassegrain designs were found which met requirements, and the lowest risk design was selected as the baseline. However, other designs have better image quality and throughput, and their perceived risks may diminish as the underlying technologies mature.  For IFS mode, delivered image quality is just as crucial, but this is achieved through NGS GLAO. The challenges come from (a) the requirement that 3'x3' subfields can be selected from the 13' diameter FoV without repointing the telescope, and (b) relaying the beam to a fixed horizontal focus under the telescope. This is done by a field-selecting pick-off at telescope focus, and large reimaging optics at Nasmyth.

Items.Authors: Jonathan W. Arenberg
Items.Title: Getting X-ray astronomy down to business: facing the manufacturing challenge
Items.Abstract: Astronomy is a technologically limited science, with x-ray astronomy providing an extreme example. Advancement of the field requires ever more sensitive observations of the universe and the systems that make these measurements are by necessity novel and developmental in some way. The funders and evaluators of these new systems demand, rightly, some level of accuracy and believability in the cost and schedule resources needed. To make these cost and schedule predictions cost models are use, which are based on interpolation. This means that the novel aspects of the design of the mission have no cost history. This paper will review recent work on how to “make the case” that future systems are producible and identify strategies to collect and use the needed data to secure the funding that powers advancement of the field. This presentation is based on the work for the development of causal cost methodology over the last decade.

Items.Authors: Junna Sugiyama, Kyohei Yamada, Bryce Bixler, Daichi Sasaki, Yuki Sakurai, Kam Arnold, Nicholas Galitzki, Akito Kusaka
Items.Title: The Simons Observatory: overview of the cryogenic half-wave plate polarization modulators
Items.Abstract: The degree-scale polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) is a key probe of primordial gravitational waves. The Simons Observatory (SO) is a ground-based CMB experiment located in the Atacama Plateau, Chile. The SO has deployed three Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) to target these angular scales, where atmospheric low-frequency noise, also known as the $1/f$ noise, is a major challenge. To mitigate atmospheric $1/f$ noise and instrumental systematics, each SAT employs a 505\,mm diameter 50\,K Cryogenic Half-Wave Plate (CHWP) polarization modulator that shifts the polarized sky signal to higher temporal frequencies, separating it from the unpolarized atmospheric emission. We present the on-site mechanical and optical performance of the three CHWPs and discuss their impact on the SO B-mode search.

Items.Authors: Riku Sato, Michitoshi Yoshida, Takashi Moriya, Chihiro Tokoku, Shinobu Ozaki, Kenshi Yanagisawa, Kentaro Motohara, Tomoya Yukino, Kensho Tanaka, Yoshito Ono, Yosuke Minowa, Yusei Koyama, Yutaka Hayano, Kumiko Morihana, Masayuki Akiyama, Masaomi Tanaka, Masami Ouchi, Yuichi Harikane, Nanae Domoto, Yuki Moritani, Masayuki Tanaka, Nozomu Tominaga, Koki Terao, Kosuke Kushibiki, Tohru Nagao, Yoshiki Matsuoka, Toru Misawa, Tomoki Morokuma
Items.Title: Development of the NIR arm of the NINJA spectrograph on Subaru Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Near-INfrared and optical Joint spectrograph with Adaptive optics (NINJA) is a  medium-resolution optical to near-infrared spectrograph designed to be optimized for  the Laser Tomography Adaptive Optics (LTAO) system at the Subaru Telescope.  Red-NINJA, the NIR arm of NINJA, is currently under development, with engineering first light targeted for 2026. The instrument covers 0.85 to 2.5 μm with nominal resolving power of R ~ 4000-5000. With the LTAO correction, the instrument is expected to reach a sensitivity of 22 AB mag (S/N = 10) in the J-band with a 2-hour exposure. The detector system, optics, and cryogenic mechanical assemblies have been installed inside the cryostat. Laboratory verification tests have been completed without significant issues, and Red-NINJA is now being prepared for transport to the summit and installation at the Subaru Telescope. We report the status of the instrument development, including results from the tests and a timeline toward on-sky commissioning.

Items.Authors: Aurelie Magniez, James Gill-Fleming, Deli Geng, James T. Wells, David Barr, John Connolly, Tom Davies, Sofia Dimoudi, Radhika Dharmadhikari, Charlotte Z. Bond, Noah Schwartz, Ben Buky, Pieter J. de Visser, Timothy J. Morris, Kieran O'Brien
Items.Title: Polychromatic Pyramid WFS (PoPy) project overview
Items.Abstract: Advanced adaptive optics (AO) systems are required for high-contrast imaging with ELT-scale telescopes. The pyramid wavefront sensor, selected for the first ELT instruments, offers high sensitivity. However, its performance varies significantly with wavelength. While the visible wavelength range provides greater sensitivity, it has a limited dynamic range and significant optical gain effects. Correcting these variations could improve temporal errors and extend the sensing waveband, enabling AO to be used with fainter targets.  Energy-resolving detectors, such as MKIDs, offer a way to measure the entire VIS-NIR spectrum without the need for multiple cameras. The PoPy project aims to demonstrate the benefits of using polychromatic measurements. Alongside simulations, we are developing a bench with an MKID array and a colour splitter for initial testing. Here, we present the initial demonstration results of a closed loop on a polychromatic WFS and provide an overview of our future plans.

Items.Authors: Gianalfredo Nicolini, Michela Uslenghi, Serena Farina, Vincenzo Andretta, Giampiero Naletto, Maurizio Pancrazzi, Marco Romoli, Luca Teriaca
Items.Title: Time and frequency domain characterisation of the Metis: Solar Orbiter coronagraph
Items.Abstract: Metis is the ultraviolet–visible coronagraph on board the ESA Solar Orbiter mission, designed to image the solar corona simultaneously in polarised visible light and in the Lyman-α ultraviolet emission. The instrument can acquire full-frame images on both channels at a very high rate, with a minimum cadence of one second. This capability enables detailed investigations of coronal variability and fluctuations, but also requires an accurate characterisation of the instrument response in both the time and frequency domains.  In this work, we present the methodology adopted to assess the temporal and spectral variability of the response of the Metis detectors. In particular, we identify and analyse the main sources of signal variability due to instrumental effects, with the aim of quantifying their impact on the measurements and decoupling them from the intrinsic physical fluctuations of the solar corona.
